stem: A sample of iron contains three different isotopes and has a relative atomic mass, $A_{r}$, of 55.8.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Table 2.1 shows the abundances of two of the isotopes present in the sample of iron.

Table 2.1

| isotope | relative isotopic mass | abundance / % |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $^{54}\text{Fe}$ | 53.9 | 6.0 |
| $^{56}\text{Fe}$ | 55.9 | 91.9 |

Use Table 2.1 to calculate the relative isotopic mass of the third isotope of iron in the sample. Show your working.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Deduce the number of pairs of electrons in the 3d sub-shell in an iron(II) ion.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Sketch the shape of the lowest energy orbital in the shell with principal quantum number $n = 2$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Complete Table 2.2 to show information about particles in one ion of $^{56}\text{Fe}^{3+}$.

Table 2.2

| particle | number of particles present in one ion of $^{56}\text{Fe}^{3+}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| electrons |  |
|  | 30 |

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
The atomic radius of iron is $1.26 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}$.

Suggest the change to the radius, if any, after an iron atom reacts to produce an $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ion. Explain your answer.
